passage_text: Researchers studied the effect of a novel dietary supplement on glucose tolerance in a cohort of 120 adults aged 30–60 years. Participants were randomly assigned to either the supplement group (n = 60) or a placebo group (n = 60). Baseline fasting glucose levels were measured, followed by an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) at 30, 60, and 120 minutes. The supplement group received 500 mg of the compound daily for 12 weeks, while the placebo group received an identical inert capsule. After the intervention period, fasting glucose and OGTT results were compared between groups. The researchers reported a mean reduction of 0.8 mmol/L in fasting glucose for the supplement group versus a 0.1 mmol/L reduction in the placebo group, with a p-value of 0.02. The OGTT curves showed a steeper decline in plasma glucose levels in the supplement group at 60 and 120 minutes. The study concluded that the supplement improved fasting glucose and glucose handling in these adults.
table_data:
Sample ID | Treatment | Fasting Glucose (mmol/L) | OGTT 60min (mmol/L) | OGTT 120min (mmol/L)
---|---|---|---|---
S1 | Supplement | 6.2 | 8.1 | 6.5
S2 | Supplement | 5.9 | 7.8 | 6.3
S3 | Placebo | 6.4 | 8.3 | 6.6
S4 | Placebo | 6.1 | 8.0 | 6.4
S5 | Supplement | 6.0 | 8.0 | 6.4
stem: Which of the following best describes the primary outcome measured in this study?
explanation: The study explicitly reports a mean reduction in fasting glucose levels as the main result, indicating that fasting glucose was the primary outcome.
trap: Option B refers to body mass index, which was not measured or reported in the study.

trap: Option A describes a study that measures exposure and outcome at a single point in time, which is not the case here.

stem: Which of the following statements is a potential trap for interpreting the study’s results?

options.A: Participants in both groups received identically appearing capsules.
options.B: The sample size was adequate to detect small differences.
options.C: The placebo group also showed a reduction in fasting glucose.

explanation: The passage gives no power calculation, and with n = 60 per group, claiming the sample was adequate to detect small differences is unsupported. The other statements are true: identical capsules were used, the placebo group did show a small reduction (0.1 mmol/L), and the study lasted 12 weeks.
trap: Assuming adequate power for small differences when none was reported.

stem: Fasting glucose change was compared between two independent groups (supplement vs placebo, n = 60 each) and reported with a p-value. Which test is most appropriate for this comparison of means?
explanation: Two independent groups with a continuous outcome are compared with an independent two-sample t-test. A paired test needs matched/repeated measures on the same subjects, and chi-square applies to categorical data.
trap: Using a paired t-test because each participant has a before and after value; the group comparison still involves two independent samples.
